Rarity tier decides the price

Dragon Ball Super Card Game runs a steep rarity ladder, and the top tiers trade far above the common printings of the same character. Secret Rare and God Rare pulls are the cards that carry a set's value.

A matching record and its available price must be confirmed before using Card AI for this category. Do not infer support from a rarity label.

Leaders and alternate art are separate positions

Leader cards and alternate art treatments trade on their own, apart from the standard version at the same card number. Keep those variants separate when matching a catalog record; coverage for them has not been confirmed.

Track a set as it moves

For supported records, Card AI can track confirmed holdings and available price history. This does not establish coverage for this release or predict future prices.

Is Dragon Ball Super coverage confirmed in Card AI?

Coverage is not confirmed for this category. Check the current card categories and an exact catalog result before relying on a scan or price.

Does a Secret Rare or God Rare label identify the exact card?

No. Match the release, full number, artwork, language and finish. A rarity name alone is not a catalog match or a price.

That coverage has not been confirmed. A language field on a supported record does not establish a complete Japanese catalog.

What if there is no matching Dragon Ball Super record?

Keep the issuer or checklist reference and do not save another printing as a substitute. A missing record or price is not evidence that your card is worth zero.
